newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom up after pricing news.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom up after pricing news.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications rallied to their highest level since September 1995 after the company said it would cut further the cost of international telephone calls.
At 0851 GMT, the shares were up 7p to 412-1/2p.
Trading volume was 1.62 million shares, making the shares the most actively traded in London.

In a statement released before the markets opened, British Telecommunications said it reduce the prices on many overseas calls, effective from February 19. The latest round of reductions will cover calls to 33 countries, accounting for 60 percent of international calls, the company said nL14230448.
Some attributed the rally to a technical breakout in the share price. They noted that the shares have risen above of their two year range, which portends a further advance.
SocGen analyst John Tysoe said he believes the stock's appreciation was not tied to price cuts or to technical factors.

"If you wanted to attach a more rational reason (for the rally), you'd have to say that the penny has finally dropped. European deregulation is less than a year away and there's only one company that's prepared to exploit that market and that's BT," said Tysoe, who repeated his "buy" recommendation on the stock this morning.
UBS also reiterated its "buy" recommendation today, dealers said.
